chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Sulayman al-Minqari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: May I be your ransom, what is upon a man who assaulted a woman and shaved her head?

He عليه السلام said: “He is to be beaten severely and imprisoned in the prison of the Muslims until her hair is ascertained. If it grows back, the mahr of women like her is taken from him; and if it does not grow back, the full diyah is taken from him.”

I said: Then how is it that the mahr of women like her is due if her hair grows back? He عليه السلام said: “O Ibn Sinan, indeed a woman’s hair and her virginity are two partners in beauty. So when one of the two is taken away, her full mahr becomes due.”

key_terms.مَهْرُ نِسَائِهَا: the mahr customarily given to women comparable to her
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ: he is to be beaten as punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man assaults a woman and shaves her head in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a man who assaults a woman by shaving her head. It establishes corporal punishment and imprisonment, then financial liability based on whether her hair regrows: the mahr of comparable women if it returns, and the full diyah if it does not. The Imam عليه السلام explains this by linking a woman’s hair with her beauty and legal compensation.
